spec_features.evidence: tools.py defines give_up (TOOL_SPECS, line ~53) and it is in _TOOL_NAMES so the parser accepts it. loop.py:44 _execute_tool handles name=='give_up' and returns is_give_up=True; loop.py:119-127 'if is_give_up: abandoned=True; ... break' actually breaks out of the turn loop. So the subject can emit give_up and the rollout loop terminates early end-to-end (dispatched AND honored as a stop).
spec_features.notes: abandoned/abandoned_turn are recorded on the Rollout and persisted, but no downstream code reads them (no report/metric uses .abandoned). The exit-as-stop itself is enforced regardless. The framed purpose (per DESIGN.md) is measuring a refusal mode, but the loop still genuinely stops.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up(reason) -> the model can explicitly abandon the task
